facts.statement: Lonchodectes is a genus of pterosaur from the Late Cretaceous of England, primarily found near Kent.
facts.quote: Lonchodectes (meaning "lance biter") is a genus of lonchodectid pterosaur from several formations dating to the Turonian (Late Cretaceous) of England, mostly in the area around Kent.

facts.statement: Lonchodectes possessed long jaws with many short teeth that were compressed vertically, resembling a pair of sugar tongs.
facts.quote: Lonchodectes had long jaws with many short teeth, and the jaws were compressed vertically, like "a pair of sugar tongs with teeth".

facts.statement: Researchers suggest that Lonchodectes compressirostris likely had crests on its lower jaws, similar to related species.
facts.quote: Related species (including several taxa formerly included within the genus) had crests on their lower jaws, so the same probably also applied to L. compressirostris.

facts.statement: The type species Lonchodectes compressirostris is based on a partial upper jaw fossil found in the Upper Cretaceous Upper Chalk near Kent.
facts.quote: The type species, L. compressirostris, is based on NHMUK 39410, a partial upper jaw from the Turonian-age Upper Cretaceous Upper Chalk near Kent.

facts.statement: The species was originally named in 1851, transferred to another genus in 1870, and finally established as the type species of Lonchodectes in 1914.
facts.quote: Richard Owen named in 1851 as a species of Pterodactylus; it was transferred to Ornithocheirus in 1870 by Harry Govier Seeley, before becoming the type species of Lonchodectes in Reginald Walter Hooley's 1914 review of Ornithocheirus.

facts.statement: In 2019, researchers suggested that the type specimen of Lonchodectes compressirostris might be the same species as Cimoliopterus cuvieri.
facts.quote: In 2019, the Brazilian palaeontologist Rubi V. Pêgas and colleagues suggested that the type specimen of Lonchodectes compressirostris could represent the same species as Cimoliopterus cuvieri.

facts.statement: In 2003, the genus was placed in the family Lonchodectidae within Ctenochasmatoidea, and later in 2006, it was placed within Azhdarchoidea.
facts.quote: In 2003, Unwin placed them in their own family, Lonchodectidae, which he grouped within the group Ctenochasmatoidea, while in 2006, he placed the family Lonchodectidae within the Azhdarchoidea, the group that includes the tapejarids and azhdarchids.

facts.statement: Recent reviews have limited the genus Lonchodectes to only its type species, L. compressirostris.
facts.quote: Therefore, Lonchodectes is limited to its type species, L. compressirostris.

facts.statement: It is debated whether Lonchodectes is a valid genus, as species were previously assigned to Ornithocheirus until the work of David Unwin.
facts.quote: The species belonging to it had been assigned to Ornithocheirus until David Unwin's work of the 1990s and 2000s.

facts.statement: The status of L. platystomus is debated, with some suggesting it may belong to the genus Amblydectes.
facts.quote: L. platystomus may be a species of Amblydectes.

facts.statement: Most potential species of Lonchodectes are known only from fragmentary remains and have undergone multiple generic reassignments.
facts.quote: Several potential species are known; most are based on scrappy remains, and have gone through several other generic assignments.

facts.statement: The genus Lonchodectes was named by Hooley in 1914.
facts.quote: PBDB name: Lonchodectes (genus), Hooley 1914

facts.statement: Lonchodectes belongs to the parent group Ornithocheiroidea.
facts.quote: Parent group: Ornithocheiroidea

facts.statement: Lonchodectes is classified within the class Reptilia.
facts.quote: Class: Reptilia

facts.statement: Lonchodectes lived from the Albian to the Turonian stages, between 113.2 and 89.8 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Albian to Turonian (113.2 to 89.8 million years ago)

facts.statement: There are 9 recorded fossil occurrences of Lonchodectes.
facts.quote: Fossil occurrences recorded: 9

facts.statement: Unwin considered Lonchodectes a generalist species similar to a gull due to its conservative jaws and teeth, estimating a maximum wingspan of nearly 2 meters.
facts.quote: Unwin considera a Lonchodectes como una especie generalista, como una gaviota, debido a sus mandíbulas y dientes más conservadores (como los del mucho más antiguo Pterodactylus) y de tamaño pequeño a medio; él estimó su envergadura máxima en cerca de 2 metros.

facts.statement: Lonchodectes had long jaws with many short teeth that were vertically compressed, resembling "a pair of sugar tongs with teeth."
facts.quote: Lonchodectes tenía largas mandíbulas con muchos dientes cortos, y las mandíbulas estaban comprimidas verticalmente, como "un par de pinzas para azúcar con dientes".

facts.statement: At least some species of Lonchodectes had crests on their lower jaw.
facts.quote: Al menos alguna de estas especies tenía crestas en su mandíbula inferior.

facts.statement: Recent studies suggest that Lonchodectes had limb proportions similar to azdarchids and may have lived in a similar way.
facts.quote: Sin embargo, estudios recientes muestran que sus proporciones de las extremidades son parecidas a las de los azdárquidos, y puede haber vivido de forma similar.

rejected.statement: A 2018 analysis placed Lonchodectes within the family Lonchodectidae as the sister taxon of Lonchodraco.
rejected.quote: In their analysis, they placed Lonchodectes within the family Lonchodectidae as the sister taxon of Lonchodraco.

rejected.statement: A 2018 analysis placed the family Lonchodectidae, including Lonchodectes, within the group Ornithocheiromorpha.
rejected.quote: Contrary to previous analyses, Longrich and colleagues placed Lonchodectidae (including Lonchodectes) within the more inclusive group Ornithocheiromorpha.
